_about: Field terms for F172, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

significance-filter.definition: the selection of published results by a significance threshold, which lets lucky overestimates through more often than underestimates, so the published effects of a set of studies are on average larger than the true ones
significance-filter.excludes: deliberate misconduct, which the filter neither requires nor detects

selection-model.definition: a model of observed results that writes down both a distribution of true effects and the rule by which results get seen, here the rule that only originals with z above 1.96 in absolute value are seen, and fits both together
selection-model.excludes: a model that takes the observed results as an unselected sample

fisher-z.definition: the transform of a correlation r to half the natural log of (1 + r) over (1 - r), on which the sampling error is close to normal with standard error 1 over the square root of n minus 3
fisher-z.excludes: the z statistic of a test, which is an effect divided by its standard error

face-value.definition: a forecast that takes each published original effect as the true effect and predicts replication from the power a replication of the given size would have against it
face-value.excludes: any correction for how the original was selected

base-rate.definition: a forecast that gives every effect in a held-out field the same chance of replicating, the share that replicated in the training fields
base-rate.excludes: any use of an effect's own statistics

brier-score.definition: the mean squared difference between a forecast probability and the outcome coded 1 or 0, from 0 for a perfect forecast to 1 for a confident wrong one; 0.25 is what a forecast of one half always earns
brier-score.excludes: a ranking measure such as AUC, which ignores whether the probabilities are at the right level

logistic-regression.definition: a model in which the log odds of success are a weighted sum of predictors, here the original z value, the log of the original sample size and the log of the replication sample size, fitted by maximum likelihood on the training fields
logistic-regression.excludes: any model of how originals were selected

leave-one-field-out.definition: a test in which each field in turn is held out, every parameter is fitted on the other fields, and forecasts are scored only on the held-out field
leave-one-field-out.excludes: scoring forecasts on the rows that were used to fit them

cluster-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by recomputing a statistic many times, here 2,000, on samples of whole replication projects drawn with replacement, so rows from one project stay together
cluster-bootstrap.excludes: resampling single rows as if they were independent

sign-flip.definition: a test that sums the per-project differences between two forecasts' scores, then flips the sign of each project's difference at random many times, here 4,000, to see how often a sum as large arises with no true difference
sign-flip.excludes: a test that treats rows inside one project as independent

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05; the adjusted values are called q values
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

bic.definition: the Bayesian information criterion, minus twice the maximised log likelihood plus the number of parameters times the log of the number of rows; lower is better, and a difference of 10 is the usual bar for strong preference
bic.excludes: a test of whether either model is right

calibration.definition: agreement between forecast probabilities and observed frequencies: among effects given a chance near 0.7, about 70 percent should replicate; checked here in five bands of equal count
calibration.excludes: discrimination, the separate question of whether higher forecasts go with more successes
